input.nbt_payload_description: well-formed gzip and enough bytes, but the very first tag-type byte is 0x03 (int) instead of 0x0A (compound)

notes: readRootCompound (line 1134-1140): `guard let type = NBTTag(rawValue: try readUInt8()), type == .compound else { throw NSError(...code: 1) }`. Every real level.dat (Java or Bedrock) is required by the format itself to start with a root compound, so this is a defensive check against garbage input (e.g. a truncated/wrong file handed in as a slot's level.dat) rather than a real-world branch MSC 1 is ever expected to hit against genuine Minecraft output -- included because the Rust port must preserve the same 'malformed root -> nil, not a crash' contract regardless of why it happens.
